parsed.hook: Black Box Deep & Dark is a 3-liter bag-in-box Cabernet Sauvignon built for everyday drinking at roughly $5 per bottle equivalent — and it punches above that math. parsed.wine_summary:
Black Box has been the most credible name in premium bag-in-box wine in the U.S. since the format gained mainstream traction in the mid-2000s. The oxygen-barrier bag technology (which collapses as wine is poured, preventing oxidation) keeps the wine fresh for up to four weeks after opening — a practical advantage no bottle can match for households that don't finish a bottle in one sitting. The Deep & Dark bottling is sourced from California broadly, which means grapes likely come from warm interior regions like Lodi or the Central Valley where warm days and high yields produce the ripe, dark-fruited Cabernet profile the label promises. No single appellation is called out, which limits what can be said about specific terroir — but it also keeps costs down in ways that matter at this price point.

The 2021 vintage earned a bronze at TEXSOM, the 2022 took gold from an unnamed panel, and the NV earned silver — a scattered but generally positive competition track record for a wine in this category. These aren't scores that suggest complexity, but they confirm consistency and drinkability, which is exactly what this wine is engineered to deliver.

parsed.food_pairing:
1. Smash burgers with American cheese — the fat in the beef softens the tannins while the wine's dark fruit amplifies the char on the patty. Classic, direct, works every time.
2. BBQ beef brisket — the smoky, fatty richness of long-smoked brisket is exactly what a ripe, soft-tannin Cab needs to find its footing. The wine's dark plum notes mirror the bark on the meat.
3. Spaghetti with meat sauce (Sunday gravy) — the tomato acidity in a long-cooked Bolognese-style sauce bridges the wine's fruit and keeps the finish from feeling heavy. Casual, weeknight-friendly.
4. Sharp cheddar and charcuterie — the salt and fat in aged cheddar and cured meats round off any rough edges in the tannin structure. Works as a no-cook option when you just want to open the box.
5. Mushroom and Swiss burger or portobello burger — the umami depth of mushrooms amplifies the wine's earthy undertones and makes the whole package feel more complex than either component alone.
parsed.comparable_wines:
Bota Box Nighthawk Black Cabernet Sauvignon — the most direct competitor in the bag-in-box category at the same price point, slightly riper and jammier in style, making Black Box Deep & Dark the more structured option of the two.
Franzia Dark Red Blend — cheaper and simpler, useful for volume occasions but without the varietal definition or competition pedigree that Black Box has built.
SonomaCutrer Russian River Ranches Chardonnay (750ml, ~$22) — not a style comp, but a price-point comparison that illustrates what $20 buys in a bottle versus a box: the Black Box delivers more wine for the money, just less provenance.
